papers.title: MemLeak: Diagnosing Information Leaks in Multimodal Agent Memory
papers.issueTitle: MemLeak: Diagnosing Information Leaks in Multimodal Agent Memory
papers.plainExplanation:
The IPG is explicitly descriptive, not an impossibility theorem. FC counts deleted representation nodes, while CMLR measures behavioral recoverability; FC=1 is not in general equivalent to zero inference from correlated retained data, a distinction the paper explicitly acknowledges. Reconstructed majority vote as at least 2/3 with ambiguous counted negative. All Table 4 count/rate pairs and Wilson intervals agree to reporting precision; the 0/300 upper Wilson bound is 1.264%, not proof of population-zero leakage. Paired cross-model partition sums to 300 and gives 89.33% agreement and 16% union. Semantic transitions 36-35+5=6 explain why new post-deletion leaks coexist with eliminating 35 baseline cases; reduction is sixfold. Category denominators sum to 300; image-only share 17/36 rounds to 47%. The 55 pilot probes versus 50 target facts is not necessarily contradictory because probes need not be unique facts; the manuscript leaves repeated-probe structure unspecified. Wilson intervals treat probes as binomial units; within-profile dependence and true deployment generalization are not established by these marginal intervals. No numerical contradiction demonstrated. Unsplash experiment is acknowledged as stock-photo realism rather than real-user deployment. No API/model or Mem0 code executed, and no independent human-judge audit conducted. papers.plainExplanation: No issue was found in the checked claims. All three appendix proofs verified line by line and found correct. Theorem 1 (concave-over-modular): normalization from h_r(0)=0, monotonicity from a_ur>=0 and h_r nondecreasing, and submodularity from the diminishing-increment property of concave h_r with z_r(S)<=z_r(T) all check out. Proposition 4: densities 2*delta/delta=2 vs 1/1=1, the one-representation-per-experience constraint (|X intersect G_i|<=1, one experience) forces OPT=1, ratio 2*delta<=eta, and the hypotheses 0<c_u<=B/2 hold (delta<=1/4<=1=B/2, c_b=1=B/2) - correct. Theorem 5: verified both cost cases (F(X)>=lambda*C(X)>=lambda*B/2>=(1-eps)OPT/4 when C(X)>=B/2), the below-threshold charge (Delta(u|X_final)<=Delta(u|X_arrival)<lambda*c_u, total <= lambda*B<=OPT/2 using lambda<=OPT/(2B) and O budget-feasible), budget-feasibility at arrival (final C(X)<B/2 and c_u<=B/2 give C(X_t)+c_u<B), and the injective mapping of threshold-admissible missed elements to accepted arrivals (O satisfies |O intersect G_i|<=1, so each group contributes at most one missed element, which maps to that group's single accepted element with marginal >= Delta(u|X_arrival)>=Delta(u|X_final); charges sum <= F(X)); conclusion OPT<=2F(X)+OPT/2, i.e. F(X)>=OPT/4, and the grid lambda in [(1-eps)OPT/(2B), OPT/(2B)] makes the C(X)>=B/2 case give (1-eps)OPT/4. The MILP certificate (y_r<=sum_u a_ur x_u, y_r<=1) is a correct epigraph formulation of h_r(z)=min(1,z). Near-misses NOT reported: (a) Table 5's ratio columns are not the ratios of the adjacent OPT columns (python3: k2/k1 computed 1.0129/1.0133/1.0343 vs printed 1.013/1.027/1.060; byte/default computed 1.4071/1.0937/1.0960 vs printed 1.322/1.107/1.131), and the main-text claim 'allowing k=2 changes exact OPT by only 1.3-6.0%' tracks the ratio column; but if the ratio columns are means of per-example ratios while the OPT columns are means of per-example OPT values, the mismatch is expected, so this is not demonstrably wrong. (b) Table 4's Letta salience-pruned package ratio 0.881 vs Table 6's word-rule 'Letta salience' 0.899 for the same B=100 comparison (Mem0's 0.489 and A-Mem's 0.000 do match across the two tables) - cannot be adjudicated without the artifact. papers.plainExplanation: Full manuscript read. Reconstruct the energy identity using hydrostatic dPhi=-Rd*T*dp/p and constant cp-cv=Rd. Integration by parts gives integral(Phi dp)=ps*Phi_s+integral(Rd*T dp), provided p*Phi tends to zero at the top. Thus integral(cv*T+Phi)=integral(cp*T+Phi_s), so the screening concern is refuted rather than a formula defect. Moist corrections and condensate omissions remain approximations, not demonstrated errors. For geostrophy, northward geopotential increase gives negative eastward geostrophic wind; longitudinal derivative has the required cos(latitude) factor. Hypsometric thickness is positive since 850/500>1; the negative sign in lapse rate gives positive lapse rate when temperature falls aloft. The CDF discrete Wasserstein formula assumes unit k spacing, which the stated integer wavenumbers provide. No formal sufficiency guarantee for physical realism is claimed; D.2 explicitly cautions against that inference. Drift units require regression time in days; Table 2 hours versus percent/day needs implementation inspection and is not confirmed. Masking partially intersected layers uses endpoint averaging rather than interpolation, an ordinary quadrature approximation. Executed output: internal+potential= 28139920000.0 enthalpy+surface= 28139920000.0 hypsometric 850-500 thickness= 42648.71505087088 CDF Wasserstein= 1.0 Remaining gaps: implementation, benchmark reruns, external revision searches and independent review not performed.

papers.title: FMMI: Flow Matching Mutual Information Estimation
papers.issueTitle: Smooth compact support is incompatible with a globally Lipschitz log density
papers.plainExplanation:
Let \(U=\{p>0\}\), choose \(y\in U\), and take its nearest boundary point \(b\). The segment from \(y\) to \(b\) lies in \(U\), while continuity gives \(p(b)=0\). A finite log-Lipschitz constant would bound \(\log p\) below on that segment by \(\log p(y)-L\|b-y\|\), contradicting its divergence to \(-\infty\). The literal hypothesis class is empty.

Reading smoothness only inside a support with a discontinuous boundary does not validate the proof: uniform density on \([0,1]\) has interior log-Lipschitz constant zero, but vector field \(\epsilon(x)=x\) gives \(|\mathbb E\operatorname{div}\epsilon|=1\). The boundary flux discarded by integration by parts is then nonzero. The literal assumptions make the affected guarantees vacuous; the permissive support-only reading loses the asserted bound. The Fisher-information Cauchy–Schwarz step and empirical estimators are not themselves refuted.

The paragraph describes e-BH as selecting the largest index $k$ satisfying the displayed partial-sum threshold. It then explicitly excludes e-BH from the implementation. Because e-values are nonnegative, a qualifying partial sum forces $k=m$ to qualify, so the stated largest-index rule rejects every hypothesis or none. papers.plainExplanation: Theorem 1 groups samples by their accuracy-curve shape. Let \(F_i(N)\) be mean accuracy at budget \(N\) in group \(i\), \(p_i\) its population fraction, and \(\mu_i\) its mean sample-optimal budget. The theorem uses endpoint gains \(\bar\Delta_i=F_i(N_{\max})-F_i(1)\), assumes \(\mu_4>\mu_i\) for \(i\ne4\), \(\bar\Delta_1=\bar\Delta_2=0\), \(\bar\Delta_5\approx0\) and \(p_4\bar\Delta_4>p_3[-\bar\Delta_3]_+\), then concludes expected budget utilization below one. The proof adds an interval-by-interval dominance condition that is absent from the theorem. It also drops the approximately zero Type-5 contribution without bounding its effect on the strict inequality.

papers.title: A Set-Sequence Model for Time Series
papers.issueTitle: Invariant quadratics can require a quadratic readout
papers.plainExplanation:
The set module first averages features computed separately for each unit, then applies a readout $\rho$. Appendix A.2 fixes the number of units $M$ and takes $\phi_2(x)=[x,\operatorname{vec}_{\mathrm{sym}}(xx^\top)]$, which records first and second empirical moments. Its quadratic-case remark says a linear readout represents every permutation-invariant quadratic of the cross-section. The preceding expressivity proposition permits a continuous readout, and its proof uses a polynomial readout.

The source states: “Taking $k=2$ recovers first and second empirical moments exactly, so any permutation-invariant quadratic statistic of the cross-section is obtained by a linear $\rho$.” A linear readout can combine the pooled first and second moments, but it cannot multiply pooled first moments. Those products are needed for quadratic interactions between different units. Permutation invariance does not remove these interactions.

papers.plainExplanation: The definition gives \(P_\theta(t)/P_d(t)=\gamma_j^{-1}P_\theta(h)/P_d(h)\). Therefore \(P_\theta(t)\leq\gamma_j^{-1}P_d(t)\) additionally requires \(P_\theta(h)\leq P_d(h)\), which is not assumed. Qualitative suppression and the odds-ratio conclusion can survive with correctly stated additional conditions.

Prop. 3.1(ii): R = Q^{-1/2}(M+I)^{-1} Q^{1/2} with M=Q^{-1/2}p(L)Q^{-1/2} succ 0 gives spectrum in (0,1) (verified symbolically). Prop. 3.1(iii): R^T=Q(P+Q)^{-1}, R=R^T <=> PQ=QP <=> (q_i-q_j)P_{ij}=0; with complete K-hop support adjacent nodes force q_i=q_j. Lemma A.2: ||p(L)R||_2 = 1/lambda_min(Q^{-1}+P^{-1}) <= p_max (since lambda_min(Q^{-1}+P^{-1}) >= lambda_min(P^{-1}) = 1/p_max); R-I=-Q^{-1}p(L)R verified. Prop. 3.2: P z = Q(x-z), q_i(x_i-z_i)^2 <= F(z) <= F(x)=x^T P x <= p_max ||x||^2 all check out. Prop. 3.3 density: the construction f=q(1-h)/h, Weierstrass p with ||p-f||_inf<q eps, and the bound |g_q-h|<=eps are correct; the non-commutativity chain [R,L]=0 <=> [Q,L]=0 and the nullspace/strict-monotonicity argument for R=g(L) => Q=qI are correct. Prop. 3.4: verified numerically on a path, a cycle and random graphs that R_{ij}=(M^{-1})_{ij} q_j and R_{ij}>0 in the same component; the cofactor monomial argument showing C_{ji} is not identically zero (unique remaining permutation is the forward shift along the minimal K-hop path) is valid. Prop. 3.5 identity R_{ij}=sqrt(q_j/q_i)(S^{-1})_{ij} verified numerically to machine precision (err ~1e-16) on path/cycle/random graphs, and the claimed bound |R_{ij}|<=2 sqrt(q_j/q_i) exp(-2 d/(K sqrt(kappa))) held in every tested instance (no violation). Prop. 3.6: from Q1^{-1}P+I=Q2^{-1}P+I and P invertible, Q1=Q2. Prop. 3.7: Delta=Q2 Q1^{-1}=P2 P1^{-1} commutes with L hence is constant per component; on each component-supported null vector p2(0)=alpha_c p1(0), so all alpha_c equal and Q2=alpha Q1, P2=alpha P1. Prop. 3.8: rank-n H has a right inverse, so R'_j=R_pi(j) and Prop. 3.7 applies channel-wise. Section 3.2 implicit differentiation: differentiating Mz=Qx gives M d_{q_i} z = E_ii(x-z), so d l/d q_i = u_i(x_i-z_i) with u=M^{-1} z-bar; verified by the matrix identity. No error found. I did not verify the empirical claims (100%/99.4% accuracy, MAE 1.17/1.20, CSBM phase-diagram) since no raw data are given; the CSBM threshold lambda^2+mu^2/gamma>1 and the weak-recovery thresholds are quoted from the cited references.

papers.title: Revisiting Value Iteration: Unified Analysis of Discounted and Average-Reward Cases
papers.issueTitle: The own-state action coefficient subtracts the discount instead of one
papers.plainExplanation:
Take the deterministic cycle \(1\to2\to3\to1\), one action per state and constant reward \(1/2\). Its sole policy is uniquely optimal and unichain, but periodic. Centered rewards and bias vanish. Starting from \(x_0=v_0/C=(2,-1,-1)\), the anchor vanishes and \(x_t=\gamma^tP^tx_0\). Since \(P^9=I\), \(\operatorname{sp}(x_9)=\gamma^9\operatorname{sp}(x_0)=3\gamma^9\), contradicting every extra factor below one. At \(\gamma=1\), values cycle.

A valid restricted argument needs a horizon \(L\) and common column \((P^{*L})_{ij}\geq b>0\) for every starting state. If every nonoptimal action also has normalized Bellman gap at most \(-\delta<0\), positive initial span permits optimal-kernel weight \(\alpha=\min\{1,\delta/\operatorname{sp}(x_0)\}\). Each interpolated \(L\)-step product then has common-column mass at least \(\alpha^Lb\), giving contraction factor \(\gamma^L(1-\alpha^Lb)\). The cycle refutes the extra strict span factor and average-reward value convergence. Its only policy is optimal, so it does not refute the policy-optimality corollary or ordinary discounted contraction. The restricted repair requires its stated hypotheses and proof.

papers.issueTitle: Environment subtraction evaluates sufficient statistics at different noises
papers.plainExplanation: At one observed \(x\), equation (35) has \(n_u=(h^u)^{-1}(f^{-1}(x))\). Subtraction gives \(T(n_\ell)^\top\eta_\ell-T(n_0)^\top\eta_0\), not \(T(n)^\top(\eta_\ell-\eta_0)\). A unit Jacobian determinant does not identify these noise arguments. For \(z_1=n_1,z_2=a(u)n_1+n_2\), the same observed \(z\) implies different noises as \(a(u)\) changes. The decoder relation being environment independent does not establish an environment-independent exogenous-noise relation. This is a Step I proof gap, not a disproof of the final causal-variable conclusion.

It is not maximum absolute sensitivity, and no theoretical gradient guarantee is claimed. For normalized vectors, routing score is r_test dot (mean harmful - mean benign), invariant to reference pairing and within [-2,2]. A suspected Table 14 FA deviation mismatch was refuted by execution: BDS mean=91.37, sample SD=.500466 rounds to .50, as printed. Ours HS mean=.075 and sample SD=.095743 round to .08 and .10. The population-SD reading is unnecessary. Screening score-selection flag is a deliberate signed-max definition, not a demonstrated computation error; universal stronger causal interpretation is not established. Then \(\operatorname{Var}(X_t)=tI_d\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid X_t)=(1-t)I_d\). The remaining target \((Y-X_t)/(1-t)\) has conditional mean zero and conditional variance \(I_d/(1-t)\). papers.issueTitle: A Locally Tokenized Generative Model for Robust Time-Series Watermarking
papers.plainExplanation: No issue was found in the checked claims. Read the complete 115,561-character text (Sections 1-4, Appendices A-E and all tables) in gapless ranges. Verified: Eq. (1)'s standardisation is exact under the stated null (variance mu0(1-mu0)/N, so sigma0 = 1/(2 sqrt N) at mu0 = 1/2, giving 0.15076, 0.12500 and 0.08839 for the 11/16/32 tokens of T = 24/64/128); N = (T-R)/s+1 reproduces from the printed hyperparameters (receptive field 4; stride 2 at T=24 and 4 at T=64,128); the attack-spread bound ceil(R/s)+1 evaluates to 3 and 2 and is conservative; the parity-alternating partition of Eq. (9) bounds a run of identical tokens to at most half of its positions lying in the biased green set, so the run's green ratio cannot saturate; the unbiased warm-up of Eq. (10) is excluded consistently at injection and detection; the subsampled-mean z-score uses the correct scaling and Phi^{-1}(0.999) = 3.0902 is the correct threshold; and the FPR and mean-z columns of Table 2 are sign-consistent on the Stocks rows (FPR 1.00 with z = +69.43 and +8.11, FPR 0.00 with z = -1.40 and -14.87). Resolved screening question 1 as answered rather than confirmed: the independence statement in Eq. (1) is an explicitly stated assumption of the detection template and not a claim about the proposed tokenizer; the printed configuration has zero window overlap at T = 64 and 128 (stride equals the receptive field) and 50% overlap only at T = 24, where the paper itself reports the resulting run structure ('adjacent windows largely overlap, so the AR Transformer frequently emits runs of the same token') and mitigates it with the parity-alternating partition; and the operational thresholds are calibrated empirically on clean non-watermarked samples at 0.1% FPR, so no reported FPR or TPR claim depends on the i.i.d. variance. A crude stand-in simulation (2-symbol quantisation of 50%-overlapping window means of an AR(1) series, N = 11, warm-up excluded) produced a null standard deviation only about 1.12x the i.i.d. value at phi = 0.95, which is not evidence of a material defect, so nothing is reported; the residual scale effect on the reported z-scores at T = 24 is recorded as a limitation. Rejected near-misses: (a) 'adjacent windows largely overlap' does not contradict the hyperparameter table, since it refers to the T = 24 configuration and to intra-window overlap of the receptive field; (b) the 3.09 threshold is the correct normal quantile rather than an approximation error; (c) the Appendix C partition comparison is qualitative and shows no internal contradiction, though its individual entries cannot be reproduced without code. Not inspected: no code repository is linked, so the tokenizer, the robust encoder E*_rho, the attacks and the calibration code are unverified, and no experiment was re-run.

papers.issueTitle: EVIDENT: Routing MLLM Adaptation through Entity-Grounded Visual Evidence for Cross-Domain Video Temporal Grounding
papers.plainExplanation: Read the complete 76,708-character text (main body, Appendices A-F, references) in gapless ranges. No theorem is present; the checkable content is four equations, the architecture record in Appendix C.3, and a large set of quoted deltas. Resolved screening question 1 as refuted: the concern was that a slot map normalised to sum to one along the token axis cannot serve as a Bernoulli probability for a multi-patch binary K-means cluster mask, so the BCE would favour concentrating on one patch. Executed check with N=64 tokens, K=4 slots, cluster size m=16: the constrained BCE minimiser is C/m (uniform on the true cluster, loss 0.6931), while putting all mass on a single patch gives infinite loss (log 0 at the other 15 positives) and a wrong cluster also gives infinite loss; a uniform map gives 1.0515. The loss therefore recovers the cluster support and the one-patch collapse is the worst configuration, not the best. The residual limitation is a positive loss floor because the map cannot encode cluster size, i.e. clusters are matched only softly - a design choice, not a false step. Also verified: softmax-over-slots followed by token-axis normalisation is exactly the cited slot-attention scheme (all slot columns sum to 1 in a toy matrix); Eq. (4) is dimensionally consistent with W_up of shape d x D and is an exact identity at initialisation; Eq. (6) is correctly bounded in [0,1] and Appendix C.3's 'substitute 1 for an absent concept' is the multiplicative identity. Arithmetic verified against the paper's own tables: 3.9 (distillation), 1.0 (gating), 5.5 and 7.2 (Table 1), -11.9 (self-attention variant), 1.4 (query-dependent gating), 2.1 (attention reuse), 2.0 lambda spread, 4.0 layer ablation, 23.9 and 19.6 point OOD drops; Appendix B.1 counts 635+915=1550 and 600+600=1200; Table 3 rows sum to 600/600 and columns to [248,248,235,233,236] = 1200; Pearson r=0.106 at n=1200 gives t=3.690 and two-sided p=2.35e-4 with R^2=0.0112, matching the printed 2.3e-4 and 1.1%; the quoted uniform slot-attention entropy bound 4.2 equals ln(64)=4.1589 for 64 tokens per frame. Near-misses rejected: (a) the '201M parameters (2.36% of the 7B backbone)' pair is inconsistent (201M/7B = 2.87%, and 2.36% of 7B is 165M; a backbone of about 8.5B would reconcile it, and Qwen2.5-VL-7B has about 8.3B), but the true trainable count depends on implementation details I could not inspect, so it is recorded as unresolved rather than reported; (b) if the Figure 3(b) quintiles are equally weighted and belong to the Table 1 Cha->QVH model, the middle three quintiles must average 59.87, above the top quintile's 52.8, so the profile is not monotone in visual distance - but the per-quintile values exist only inside the figure, so no error is demonstrable; (c) the sentence 'g_t is high only when both entities are present' is relative rather than absolute because min-max normalisation assigns 1 to the per-video argmax; the paper never fixes an absolute threshold, so this is withdrawn. Not inspected: no code repository is linked in the text, and no experiment was re-run.

papers.title: Parameter symmetries determine representational geometry in overparameterized nonlinear networks
papers.issueTitle: Parameter symmetries determine representational geometry in overparameterized nonlinear networks
papers.plainExplanation: Truncation cuts off the converse direction of Proposition B.15 (the auxiliary-parameterization construction that takes a parameterization with matching (β_q, r) to one symmetry-equivalent to the original) just at the point where it is about to extract zero-neuron groups from η. The forward direction of the proof is fully present and I verified every listed symmetry: (a) Permutation: permutes neurons, β_q invariant. (b) Positive scaling (α>0): ‖αw_j‖(a_j/α)=‖w_j‖a_j, β_q invariant. (c) Sign-flip: exchanges orientations and (depending on even/odd σ) flips or preserves readout, so β_q invariant. (d) Zero/duplicate/constant neuron groups preserve β_q by definition. (e) Aligned/opposite group (Def. B.7): all incoming vectors are ±w, so ‖w_k‖=‖w‖ for all k∈K, and the contribution ‖w‖·Σ a_k = ‖w‖·a^± is invariant — the proof's equality Σ‖w_k‖a_k = ‖w‖Σ a_k is therefore correct, not the 'sign-error' a first read might suggest. Proposition 5.1 (RSM decomposition) verified by direct algebra: H=diag(α)D_ν[F;U], so H^TH=[F;U]^T diag(α²_repeated) [F;U] = Σ_ℓ γ_ℓ g_ℓ g_ℓ^⊤ with γ = D_ν^⊤α². The remaining propositions' proofs (Sections D, E, F) are not in the batch file. The main-text statement 'every strictly positive γ is realizable' in Proposition 5.1 is slightly imprecise — it should be qualified with 'consistent with the duplication pattern' (since entries of γ at the ν_j copies of row j are forced equal to α_j²) — but the intended meaning is clear and the proof sketch in §5.1 acknowledges that duplication fixes integer multiplicities. No demonstrable mathematical error found in the available proof text.

papers.title: ROTATE: Regret-driven Open-ended Training for Ad Hoc Teamwork
papers.issueTitle: Current-ego regret maximization does not prove fixed-observer strict novelty
papers.plainExplanation: The novelty definition fixes observer \(t\) and requires a future artifact with strictly larger regret than the current one. In a one-step two-action coordination game, deterministic teammate \(T\) can already have regret \(1\) against fixed observer \(H\), the global maximum. No future teammate can have strictly greater regret. Maximization against a different, updated ego cannot overcome that fixed-observer bound. The strict novelty proof fails independently of a particular cycling trace. Empirical diversity, competence and increasing evaluation returns are not disproved.

papers.plainExplanation: No issue was found in the checked claims. Every load-bearing lemma, definition, and theorem in the appendix was verified line by line. The key observation that makes the depth-overhead P_D = O(D^2) work is Lemma 3.5: the recursive product prod_{j=i+1}^D (1 + Lambda_pre/alpha_j) is bounded because for alpha_j = (j+1)^2, sum_j 1/(j+1)^2 < infinity, so the infinite product converges to a constant depending only on Lambda_pre. Combined with max_{i<=D}(1+alpha_i) = O(D^2), this gives P_D = O_{Lambda_pre, Lambda_gap}(D^2). The active-call localization in Proposition B.10 is also clean: the per-edge cap k_i <= k_{i-1} ensures rho_{k_{i-1}} <= rho_{k_i}, and the max recursion Delta_{x_i}^{eff} = max{Delta_{x_{i-1}}^{eff}, |V*(x_i) - V*(x_{i-1})|} is bounded by max{2 rho_{k_{i-1}}, rho_{k_i}} <= 2 rho_{k_i}, giving C_act(D) = 2 (depth-independent). The biased-slow-oracle extension (Theorem 3.7) is also tight: the inflation by xi (not 2 xi or more) works because the slow sample's mean is V*(v) + b_v with |b_v| <= xi, so widening the slow confidence radius by xi absorbs the bias; the bound does not accumulate with depth because each level of recursion has the same fixed offset xi, not a per-level additive bias. Theorem 3.8 (loose fast-oracle envelope) is straightforward: hat B(h) >= B(h) means I_v^F widens, so I_v^loc may be wider but is still valid. The truncated Theorem 3.6 full proof is in Appendix B.6 which was cut off in the file; I verified the proof sketch in the main text and all building-block lemmas (B.2-B.14) but could not check the very end of the proof. The algorithm pseudo-code (Algorithms 1-5) is consistent with the analysis. The only thing I did not numerically verify is the experimental Table 1 numbers (which are reported, not derived).

papers.title: Artificial Aphasias in Lesioned Language Models
papers.issueTitle: Artificial Aphasias in Lesioned Language Models
papers.plainExplanation:
No issue was found in the checked claims; one count could not be reconciled without the experiment manifest. The paper states no theorem. Its lesioning (zeroing a fraction s of units without rescaling) is a deliberate intervention, not a dropout bug, and the symptom profiles, paired FFN-minus-attention vectors, bootstrap and permutation tests measure what the tables say they measure.

Reproduced: the Fisher exact test (50/306 versus 0/255, p = 1.06e-14, reported as about 1.1e-14), the depth difference 0.521 - 0.226 = 0.295 and the symptom-count gap 0.095. Open points: the stated design gives 2,520 lesion profiles and 360 strata, while the manuscript reports 2,528 profiles, which may reflect eight supplementary records; the listed category correlations do not reproduce the pooled 0.521 under a simple pair-weighted mean, so the pooling rule should be checked against the authors' script. A Figure 1B caption threshold is a typo for ratio minus one, and the claimed 81% tuning reduction cannot be recomputed from the grouped counts. Bootstrap intervals measure variation within the fixed assay, not uncertainty across model families.

papers.issueTitle: Denoising Distances in Metric Measure Spaces
papers.plainExplanation: No false or unjustified statement could be demonstrated. Verified by line-by-line algebra: (i) the Lemma 1.6 reduction to the SBM Proposition A.1 (p-q = s*gamma*r0, (p-q)^2/p*n/k ~ s*n*phi(r0)*r0^2, p*n/k ~ s*n*phi(r0), p(t)=a+gamma(r0-t)_+ is non-increasing and gamma-bi-Lipschitz, ball-mass inequality 1/k >= phi(t)); (ii) Lemma A.3's stated conclusion p/2 <= alpha <= p (alpha = log((1-q)/(1-p))/log(p(1-q)/(q(1-p)))); (iii) Lemma 4.3 (average/tail-radius derivation, Markov step, 1-window-safe average radius); (iv) Lemma 5.1/Prop 5.2 constants (p(0)-3Lp*rho <= phat(0) <= p(0)+Lp*rho, Delta_rho=4Lp*rho, pbar(U) >= p(0)-8Lp*rho); (v) Prop 7.1/7.2 (b_ref=2(q_ref*n+L_fail) <= phi*n/4, b_ref >= (sqrt(q*n)+sqrt(L_fail))^2, cluster ratio 4b/(phi*n)); (vi) Lemma 9.1 deterministic inclusions and the (l_p/(128 L_p), 1/8)-fuzzy-window property; (vii) Theorem 9.2 -> 9.4 constant bookkeeping (bar r = r/c, rbar^{-2} = c^2 r^{-2}, (1/2)phi(rbar)(n/6-1) >= (1/13)phi(r)n for n>=84 since 13/168 > 1/13). NEAR-MISS (deliberately NOT reported): in the proof of Lemma A.3 (batch lines ~3877-3886) the upper bound on alpha is written as alpha <= [Delta/(1-p)]/[Delta/p + Delta/(1-p)] = p; the denominator lower bound Delta/p + Delta/(1-p) is not implied by the two stated ingredients (log(p/q) >= Delta/p and Delta <= log((1-q)/(1-p))), and the natural combined lower bound is Delta/p + Delta/(1-q) < Delta/p + Delta/(1-p). The displayed inequality is nevertheless TRUE whenever p <= 1/2 (put h(q)=log(p/q)+log((1-q)/(1-p))-Delta/(p(1-p)); h(p)=0 and h'(q) = -1/(q(1-q)) + 1/(p(1-p)) < 0 for q<p<=1/2, so h>0; verified numerically over p<=0.5 with zero violations), and c_sbm is a free constant that can be taken <=1/2, so the lemma is true and the step is repairable with a one-line fix. Since the displayed claim is true in the intended regime (unlike a genuinely false bound), I did not report it. LIMITATION: the batch extraction truncates this paper in the middle of the proof of Lemma 3.2 (right after the union bound), so the final steps of Lemma 3.2 and any material after it that was not otherwise reproduced were not audited; Appendices A-C were present and audited.

papers.issueTitle: TurboVGGT: Fast Visual Geometry Reconstruction with Adaptive Alternating Attention
papers.plainExplanation:
No demonstrated false mathematical or numeric claim; routing-gradient implementation remains unresolved.

Equation2 maps each token feature through an MLP to M_k channels, with an M-by-M_k bias; W_i transpose times x_i correctly gives M_k-by-D representative tokens. Concatenating representatives yields Kc=sum_i floor(M*(1-k_i)) plus global/reference tokens; dense-query attention score complexity is O(L*M*Kc*D). For a fixed ratio this matches O(L²*M²*(1-k)) with D suppressed. Compression itself costs O(L*M²*(1-k)*D), so ignoring it is justified only in the stated long-sequence regime. The method remains quadratic in frame count, merely with a smaller constant; no linear-time inference guarantee is claimed.

Screening hard-routing gradient question: softmax alone yields probabilities, not a selected scalar ratio. A hard argmax dispatch and selected constant regularizer have zero gating derivative almost everywhere. However a probability-weighted retained-fraction objective and straight-through or soft-mixture reconstruction path repair the intended end-to-end mechanism; the manuscript does not specify which was used. Without implementation, this is an important reproducibility gap, not a demonstrated defect in the trained model. Executed example gives the expected-cost logit gradient and verifies its sign favors higher sparsity. Entropy minimization also encourages decisive choices, provided the missing sum over branch probabilities is understood. No top-k/compression normalization is mathematically required for the learned linear aggregation.

Printed timing ratios support approximate2–4x VGGT and1.4/2.1x FastVGGT comparisons; pi and Map backbone speedups also reproduce. ScanNet row means agree within displayed rounding (10.6667s to10.7s; .409667 to.410). Table6 FPS times table1 dense latency imply roughly315–317 frames, consistent within timing rounding and workload variation; no false matched-frame claim inferred. Best quality is qualified as competitive and some metrics are explicitly worse, so not converted into universal dominance. Caption1000-frame7/11/18x claims require plotted raw timings not available as text, not independently validated. No GPU code, gate estimator, profiler, evaluation scripts, data split, model checkpoint or training run inspected. papers.title: Flash-KMeans: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact K-Means
papers.issueTitle: Flash-KMeans: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact K-Means
papers.plainExplanation:
No substantive demonstrated algorithmic defect; exactness verified in real arithmetic with floating-point aggregation caveats.

Online argmin is associative when ties are consistently resolved and all valid centroids are visited; a 103-point random test reproduces direct Lloyd assignments exactly. Sorting indices preserves membership and segment sums add to the same cluster sufficient statistics; count and sum comparison passes to roundoff. At most occupiedK+ceil(N/BN)-1 partial segments exist, establishing the stated O((K+ceil(N/BN))*d) atomic upper bound even when clusters are empty. Empty-cluster centroid policy is unspecified but a standard carry-forward or reseeding convention repairs division by zero. Exact means standard Lloyd/no approximate nearest-neighbor or coreset, not bit-identical floating point across summation orders.

Screening IO concern: the actual CTA loop scans C for each point tile, so absent cache reuse centroid traffic can be ceil(N/BN)*K*d. The paper explicitly qualifies the one-read claim as ideal streaming; it is a cache-fit/reuse idealization, not a proven unrestricted HBM bound. The robust guaranteed benefit is removal of the N*K distance intermediate. Screening contention concern: a hot cluster spanning chunks still receives multiple global atomic merges. Thus elimination should be read as reduction of the dominant per-token contention, consistent with the low-contention algorithm heading; no claim that all atomics vanish is needed for the speedups. These limitations are recorded, not promoted to algorithm counterexamples.

Printed latency ratios reproduce approximate21.2/6.3/10.5 speedups; 94.4% corresponds17.86x. Code URL is supplied but no implementation or H200 profiler was inspected, so effective precision, tie policy, actual cache reuse, fixed-centroid global accumulation between out-of-core chunks, and time-to-first-run methodology remain unverified. No empirical speedup was independently reproduced. Remaining gaps: no code/benchmark rerun, external revision search, or independent reviewer.

papers.issueTitle: CM2: Reinforcement Learning with Checklist Rewards for Multi-Turn and Multi-Step Agentic Tool Use
papers.plainExplanation:
CM2 is an empirical training recipe without theorem guarantees. Eq. (2) awards a weighted reward when an item first becomes satisfied after its dependencies; the explicitly stated one-flip convention makes the sum of each item at most one and establishes R in [0,1] using normalized nonnegative weights and turn averaging. A nonmonotone raw judge would allow repeated rewards (the executed 0,1,0,1 example yields 2), but the authors explicitly say items only flip once, so latching satisfaction is the intended repair and this is not reported as a contradiction. Backfilled rewards intentionally attribute future success to every still-eligible prior step and are confined to the step-level variant; they are not claimed to be a potential-based shaping preserving optimal policies. Eq. (10) is undefined on an empty eligible set; this occurs once all items pass or no remaining item has satisfied dependencies. Masking those steps or assigning zero is a straightforward missing convention, and the paper neither asserts eligibility is always nonempty nor uses this variant in the final model. Screening question therefore remains implementation-unclear, not a substantive catalogued defect. Appendix .3 sets normalization denominator to 1, resolving zero group-variance concerns. Missing later turns after early termination also require a mask convention not specified in the text. Main trajectory-level final method avoids these step-specific ambiguities. papers.issueTitle: The softmax condition number omits selected rows from its maximum
papers.plainExplanation: Let \(U=\sum_{j\notin\Omega}z_j|y_j|\). Selected rows have absolute row sum \(U\), while unselected row \(i\) has \(U+(1-2z_i)|y_i|\). If selected rows exist, the correction must therefore be \(\max\{0,\max_{i\notin\Omega}(1-2z_i)|y_i|\}\). Omitting zero loses the selected-row maximum when an unselected probability exceeds one half. The general row-maximum formula is incomplete. Particular examples with nonnegative corrections and the separate softmax proposition are not refuted.

papers.plainExplanation:
Official page redirects to loc/sydney. Actual reviewed full-text URL is the unversioned arXiv HTML, distinct from the identity page.
All actual technical appendices and both promised proofs are present. No specifically promised missing technical material identified in the text.
Proposition 1 correctly uses sum_i w_i KL(q||p_i)=KL(q||p_PoE)-Z. The explicitly positive softmax teacher probabilities, normalized nonnegative weights and finite vocabulary make the consensus defined and the minimizer unique, including boundary candidate q. Proposition 2 correctly sums weighted AM-GM and states equality only for the positive-weight teachers. Zero-weight teachers do not need to agree.
A source-pinned local numerical check of the KL decomposition with three conflicting teachers, an arbitrary interior candidate, all three vertices and the PoE target passed to floating-point precision. This supplements direct algebra reading; it is not independent verification or a general proof.
The default beta=0.5 JSD is bounded by log(2) per token. The paper does not supply a separate quantified neural-parameter gradient or optimizer convergence theorem, and the two formal propositions concern the target distribution and normalization, not universal preservation of designability. No contradiction was found in those explicitly scoped propositions; empirical designability claims were not upgraded to mathematical guarantees.
Table 1 percentage claims recompute to 14.82 percent pLDDT, 16.95 percent solubility, 54.17 percent thermostability, 83.73 percent PPL reduction, 9.41 percent Novelty-T gain, and HV improvements 34.78/40.91/67.57 percent against the named baselines. The stated 31.2/3.86 minute comparison is about 8.083 times. Table 3 stated point differences also match the displayed values. No numerical mismatch retained.
Novelty-T uses each baseline own training set as explicitly disclosed; Novelty-U uses a shared reference. The text also discloses the inverse-folding task difference for MoMPNN. These were not recast as hidden protocol defects. Appendix C.2 provides an independent ProGen2 PPL check, addressing the immediate concern about dependence on the ProtGPT2 evaluator. The computational-oracle and absence-of-wet-lab limitation are explicit.
HV definitions use union-wide min-max normalization and the dominated volume from the zero reference point. The provided expressions are internally coherent for nonconstant evaluated metrics. Novelty, PPL, ProTrek cosine, averaged confidence/error scores and temperature/sampling distinctions were screened; the original metric implementation, generation samples and figure fronts were not executed or inspected.
No tentative proof/formula/statistics question was retained in this initial screen. This is not a verified-correct verdict. No independent confirmation, source-code/model execution, raw-data/generation-run audit, original-PDF/figure-pixel comparison or accepted-version check. The source heading says August 24, 2026; primary arXiv version dates and possible review-period correction flags are tracked in the version ledger after synchronization. Exact audited revision of the unversioned HTML remains unknown. The full text was read.

papers.issueTitle: Welch’s test detects mean shifts rather than every distributional action effect
papers.plainExplanation: A one-step random walk can have baseline absolute action equally \(0.25\) or \(0.75\), and intervention absolute action uniform on \([0,1]\). The summary distributions differ but both means are \(0.5\), with positive variances. Welch’s mean test therefore need not reject with probability tending to one; its rejection probability stays at its null level under the usual calibration. The distributional-sensitivity condition is insufficient for this chosen test. Single-dimension construction avoids multiple-testing complications; empirical performance is not refuted.

papers.title: WASD: Wasserstein-based Knowledge Distillation for Large Language Models
papers.issueTitle: WASD: Wasserstein-based Knowledge Distillation for Large Language Models
papers.plainExplanation: No issue was found in the checked claims. Verified the algebra of the core derivations and recomputed every reported table average with python3. (i) Entropic OT dual (Eq. 7/14) and optimal primal form Eq. 8 are the standard Sinkhorn dual/plan; substituting the optimum gives Lemma 1 with the 'minus epsilon' term exactly because the optimal plan has total mass 1. (ii) Proposition 2 is a correct application of the envelope/Danskin theorem (only the student marginal term depends explicitly on theta; the additive dual-potential ambiguity cancels because sum_i grad q_i = 0). (iii) Theorem 3 factor check: grad D(p,q) = phi*(p,q).grad q, and the self-term contributes (1/2)*grad D(q,q) = (1/2)*2 phi*(q,q).grad q, so the combined coefficient is phi*(p,q) - phi*(q,q) exactly as Eq. 26/11; the symmetric-cost choice phi*=psi* in the self-transport problem is valid (the problem is invariant under transposing P, and the dual opt set is convex). (iv) I checked that the paper's Dtilde (entropy H(P)=-sum P(log P -1)) and the standard entropically-regularised OT give the same Sinkhorn divergence after self-correction: the extra -epsilon constant and the q,p log-terms cancel exactly in Eq. 6. (v) Table 2 and all three blocks of Table 3 average correctly (e.g. KL row 85.86/5=17.172 -> 17.17; WASD Table 2 112.36/5=22.472 -> 22.47; GPT-2 XL->Base WASD 120.12/5=24.024 -> 24.02). Near-misses deliberately not reported: the claim 'under suitable conditions on the transport cost the Sinkhorn divergence is nonnegative and 0 iff p=q' is hedged and the required conditions on a cosine cost matrix are not stated, but I could not demonstrate the statement false; the reported 23.46 (AMiD) and 29.30 (AMiD, OpenLLaMA2) differ from the means of the displayed rounded cells (23.454, 29.294), which is ordinary rounding of unrounded values, not an error.

Sampling one of \(mN\) coordinates and multiplying its residual by \(mN\) gives \(mN\sum_j\mathbb E[(Y_j-y_j)^2]\), not an unamplified noise sum. papers.title: Learning Orthonormal Bases for Function Spaces
papers.issueTitle: Hilbert–Schmidt rotations need not contain an eigenbasis
papers.plainExplanation:
Every admissible rotation satisfies \(Q-I\) Hilbert–Schmidt. Let \(A=V\operatorname{diag}(2^{-i})V^*\), where \(V\) rotates every consecutive basis pair by \(\pi/4\). This is positive trace-class with simple spectrum. Every coordinate of every eigenvector has magnitude at most \(1/\sqrt2\), so any signed and permuted eigenbasis satisfies \(\|(Q-I)e_i\|^2\geq2-\sqrt2\) for every \(i\), contradicting the Hilbert–Schmidt requirement.

Finite-prefix rotations are admissible and approach objective \(\sum_i4^{-i}=1/3\). An attained optimum would have to diagonalize \(A\): admissible planar variations eliminate off-diagonal entries and order the diagonal entries. Hence this example has a supremum without an admissible maximizer. The unconditional existence and diagonalization claims fail. A characterization explicitly conditional on an existing maximizer is not contradicted.

papers.issueTitle: KL between continuous token collections needs a probability model
papers.plainExplanation: KL requires two probability measures on a shared measurable space. A token collection can induce empirical point masses, a Gaussian approximation, a categorical distribution or other models, each yielding a different divergence. The loss is underdefined as written. The presence of a VAE elsewhere does not specify a Gaussian law for every VLA token, and no actual implementation is judged.

papers.plainExplanation: Equation (8) minimizes minus the logarithm of relative success gain \(g=(f_t-f_{t-1})/f_{t-1}\), with success probabilities otherwise unconstrained. papers.plainExplanation: Let half the prompts always be correct with confidence \(1\); on the other half, two iid paths choose two wrong labels fairly. The separate strict-loss conformal-risk theorem is not challenged.

papers.title: Explaining and Preventing Alignment Collapse in Iterative RLHF
papers.issueTitle: Compact constrained optima need not satisfy the unconstrained sensitivity formula
papers.plainExplanation: Take a single prompt, \(Y\in\{0,1\}\), \(P_\theta(Y=1)=\theta\in[1/4,3/4]\), reward \(r_\phi=\phi\), parameter domain \([0,1]\), utility \(2+Y\), and squared loss \((\phi-(2+Y))^2/2\). The loss is smooth and one-strongly convex; its unconstrained minimizer is \(2+\theta\), so its constrained minimizer is always \(1\), with derivative zero. The printed inverse-Hessian formula instead gives derivative one, using a stationarity equation that fails at the boundary. At the symmetric reference policy, the KL derivative is zero, so the total-gradient claim is affected too. Compactness and strong convexity give uniqueness, not interiority. The boundary issue affects the cited lemma and related proposition/theorem uses, not every interior-instance derivation.

Distinct target-centered references can be collinear, making \(D\) rank one even when the number of references equals the ambient dimension. Projected components are then deterministically proportional, so their covariance and every conditional covariance share a nonzero null vector. Gradient noise added before projection cannot remove that deterministic relation. The ordinary-inverse evaluation formulas lack a condition. Conditional-law sufficiency itself is not refuted; a support-based formulation can handle degeneracy.

papers.title: RESIST: Resilient Decentralized Learning Using Consensus Gradient Descent
papers.issueTitle: RESIST: Resilient Decentralized Learning Using Consensus Gradient Descent
papers.plainExplanation: No issue was found in the checked claims. Let u=1/M times the all-ones vector, Q_k^pi=1 c_k^T, P=1 u^T. Row stochasticity gives c_k>=0 and sum c_k=1, so ||Q_k^pi-P||_2=sqrt(M)||c_k-u||_2<=sqrt(M-1), for every M>=1. Equation (20) identifies T=gradient F(W). Let What=1 what^T, Wstar=1 wstar^T, and Wtilde have rows w_jstar. Since each local minimizer is unconstrained, gradient F(Wtilde)=0. L-smoothness and the Frobenius triangle inequality give ||T||_F<=L(||W-What||_F+||What-Wstar||_F+||Wstar-Wtilde||_F)<=L[sqrt(sum_l (xi_l^1)^2)+sqrt(M)xi^6+Delta]<=L[sum_l xi_l^1+sqrt(M)xi^6+Delta]. Hence xi_k^4<=sqrt(M-1)L[sum_l xi_l^1+sqrt(M)xi^6+Delta]. These three coefficients are respectively no larger than (sqrt(M)+2)sqrt(2), (sqrt(M)+2)M, and sqrt(M)+2 in (34). This proves (34) without changing its coefficients, for arbitrary M,d and coordinate-dependent stochastic weights.
